insights.topic: Daily rewards / login streaks — Roblox ships this as an official first-party package, so it is table stakes, not a differentiator
insights.detail: Roblox's own Creator Hub distributes an 'Engagement Rewards' feature package with client+server logic and default UI. It has two reward types: Time (playtime-based) and Daily. Docs state 'Daily rewards unlock after a certain number of consecutive daily logins,' with configurable escalation (example given: potions on day 1 → consumables → a durable item like a new fishing rod after seven straight days). Config flags include isHiddenOnJoin (auto-popup on login) and isAlignedToStreakResetTime (24h-exact vs midnight reset). Implication for the chess auto-battler: do NOT build this from scratch — drop in the package and spend the effort on the reward *contents* (units/cosmetic shards). Note: Roblox does NOT publish a retention rationale or uplift number in these docs; the retention claim is inference, not measured.
insights.evidence: Roblox Creator Hub docs describe the package, both reward types, the consecutive-login definition, the day-1→day-7 escalation example, and the two config flags. No retention statistics stated in the docs.

insights.topic: Unit/collection completion — the single highest-leverage hook for a unit-drafting auto-battler; Pet Simulator 99 is the scale proof
insights.detail: Pet Simulator 99 (Preston/BIG Games) is built entirely on 'collect them all': the dev-authored description says '✨ Currently 2,000+ pets to collect! 🐾'. Live stats: 163,141 CCU, 2,557,680,996 visits, 2,181,278 favorites. Sol's RNG is the pure-collection variant — description: 'Roll for 400+ unique auras... How rare can you go?' — 31,010 CCU, 2,021,766,540 visits, 982,669 favorites. Both prove that an index/dex of hundreds-to-thousands of ownable entities sustains billions of visits. For a chess-piece auto-battler this maps directly: N variants per piece type (pawn/knight/bishop/rook/queen/king) × rarity tiers = a completion grid the player can never finish, which is exactly the point. Number of collectibles is the retention surface area.
insights.evidence: Live figures pulled from games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=3317771874,5361032378 on 2026-07-23. Collection framing quoted from dev-authored game descriptions returned by the same API.

insights.topic: Gacha/RNG pull as the core loop itself — Sol's RNG shows the pull CAN be the whole game, no combat needed
insights.detail: Sol's RNG (Sol's Studio) reduced the loop to: press Roll → get an aura → repeat. Dev description lists the full addiction stack explicitly: 400+ auras of varying rarity, craft gear from collected auras, 'drink potions to increase your luck and chase rare finds', and 'compete with friends for the rarest auras'. 31,010 CCU / 2.02B visits / 982,669 favorites as of 2026-07-23. Design lesson for the open monetization question (cosmetics-only gacha vs. units-in-gacha): Sol's RNG proves rarity chase alone is retentive, and its luck-potion layer is the paid accelerant pattern — sell the *luck multiplier / extra pull*, not the guaranteed unit. That keeps the pull loop intact while dodging the pay-to-win problem of selling combat units directly.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites from games.roblox.com API 2026-07-23. Loop and luck-potion mechanic quoted from dev-authored description.

insights.topic: DIRECT GENRE COMP: 'The Battle Bricks' is a Roblox unit-draft auto-battler and it appears in Roblox's own Top Revisited sort
insights.detail: The Battle Bricks (universeId 3913007563, place 10834586502) — dev description: 'a single-player tower defense styled game where you send units to defeat enemy bases to progress through stages... Discover the seemingly countless amount of units along the way with varying purposes and upgrade them enough to see their alternative forms!' Explicitly says gameplay is inspired by The Battle Cats. Live: 7,420 CCU, 122,344,256 visits, 286,168 favorites (2026-07-23). Read: a unit-collection auto-battler on Roblox is nowhere near Brookhaven scale (7k vs 519k CCU), but it over-indexes on RETURN RATE, which is the metric the algorithm rewards and the metric DevEx income depends on. Its retention hooks are chapter progression + unit-discovery + evolution ('alternative forms').

insights.topic: CAUTION — gacha unit-collection games decay violently on Roblox. Anime Defenders is the cautionary corpse
insights.detail: Anime Defenders (the flagship gacha tower-defense, closest structural cousin to a draft-units-and-place auto-battler) has 3,429,954,291 lifetime visits and 912,516 favorites but only 394 CCU as of 2026-07-23. Anime Vanguards holds better at 10,012 CCU on 1,998,946,337 visits and 1,972,772 favorites. Anime Adventures (search result 'AA', universe 3183403065) sits at ~137 CCU on 721,586 upvotes. Pattern: gacha-unit games spike enormously then collapse ~99%+ from peak once the unit meta staleness sets in and the whale cohort completes its collection. This is the #1 risk to the project's 'REAL income via DevEx' goal — visits are a lifetime-cumulative vanity number; CCU is the truth. Mitigation implied by the survivors: continuous new-unit cadence + seasonal resets (see the ranked-ladder insight) rather than a finite unit roster.
insights.evidence: Live CCU vs lifetime visits pulled 2026-07-23: Anime Defenders 394 CCU / 3.43B visits; Anime Vanguards 10,012 CCU / 2.00B visits; AA ~137 CCU. The visits-to-CCU ratio gap is the decay evidence. Peak-CCU figures for these titles were not verified in this pass, so the specific '99% from peak' magnitude is an inference from the ratio, not a measured decline.

insights.topic: Rank ladders with SEASONAL RESET — manufactured re-grind, proven in RIVALS and Blade Ball
insights.detail: RIVALS (universe 6035872082): 202,868 CCU, 16,777,710,440 visits, 84,758,705 favorites (2026-07-23) — the favorites number is the highest in this entire research set. RIVALS runs discrete Ranked Seasons (Season 0 launched Feb 28 2025; Seasons 1 'Warp', 2 'Polar', 3 'Fame' followed), each lasting roughly 2-3 months, with exclusive rewards keyed to highest rank reached and soft placement carry-over (finishing Nemesis raises the odds of placing Diamond next season). Blade Ball (13,344 CCU, 6,286,424,436 visits, 12,670,791 favorites) resets every player's Elo to Rookie at season start and gates unique Sword Skins behind Champion rank / global leaderboard placement. For a chess auto-battler this is the most native-fitting hook of all — chess players already accept Elo. Season reset + rank-gated cosmetic sword/piece skin = a recurring 2-3 month re-engagement engine that also feeds the cosmetics monetization line.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites are [High] confidence from the games.roblox.com API on 2026-07-23. The season structure, Elo reset, and rank-gated skins come from community wikis (Blade Ball Wiki, Roblox Rivals Wiki), not primary dev sources — mechanic existence is well-corroborated, but no published retention uplift exists.

insights.topic: Trading / player-run economy — the strongest long-tail retention hook on Roblox, and it costs the developer nothing to run
insights.detail: The two oldest survivors in the top-CCU list are both trading economies. Adopt Me!: 261,565 CCU, 44,196,888,255 visits, 29,358,128 favorites. Murder Mystery 2: 296,610 CCU, 27,585,712,989 visits, 22,972,534 favorites — a 2014-era game still at ~297k CCU in 2026. MM2's trade UX is deliberately friction-light (walk up to a player, press Trade, each side adds up to 4 items, both confirm twice). The retention engine is that item values are community-determined and volatile, spawning an entire third-party value-list ecosystem (Traderie, BloxSwaps, MM2Checker, Dexerto value lists) that lives OUTSIDE the game and pulls players back in. Scarcity is enforced by never re-releasing top items (Nik's Scythe, Ancient tier, only ever given to the creator and a few trusted players). Caveat for this project: trading + paid gacha in the same game is exactly the loot-box-with-cash-out structure that draws regulator and Roblox-policy attention with a young audience. If trading ships, restrict it to cosmetics and keep paid-pull items untradeable.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites [High] from games.roblox.com API 2026-07-23. Trade UX details and the value-list ecosystem are from secondary trading guides/wikis, not primary sources; the regulatory caveat is my own risk assessment, not a cited finding.

insights.topic: Limited-time events run on a PUBLISHED WEEKLY CALENDAR — Grow a Garden's 'Admin Abuse' is the current state of the art
insights.detail: Grow a Garden 2 is the #2 game on Roblox right now: 464,175 CCU, 1,365,613,891 visits in a short lifetime, 621,487 favorites (2026-07-23). Its headline retention device is 'Admin Abuse' — a developer/staff member joins a live public server and spawns rare seeds, triggers weather events, and hands out exclusive items. It runs on a fixed, publicly known weekly cadence: main event Saturdays (~1 hour), plus 'Watering Wednesday' midweek and occasional 'Stormy Sundays'. Seed/gear/egg shops get manual restocks during the window. The mechanic is FOMO plus a schedule — players set their week around it, and an entire third-party ecosystem of countdown/schedule sites exists to serve it. Transplant for the auto-battler: a fixed weekly 1-hour window where a dev spawns a limited board modifier or a guaranteed high-rarity pull. Cheap to run, no new systems, generates the CCU spike that feeds the Discover algorithm.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites [High] from games.roblox.com API 2026-07-23. Event cadence (Saturday main, Watering Wednesday, Stormy Sundays, ~1hr, manual shop restocks) comes from the Grow a Garden Fandom wiki and multiple aggregator sites, not a primary dev post — heavily corroborated but secondary.

insights.topic: Timegated upgrades / offline progression — Grow a Garden's 'grows while you're offline' plus shop-restock timers is the purest example
insights.detail: Grow a Garden 2's dev-authored description states the loop verbatim: 'Buy seeds from the shop when they restock🛒 / Plant them in your farm and watch them grow🌻 / Harvest your crops and sell for sheckles🪙' and closes with 'Remember, your garden literally grows while you're offline!⏰'. Two distinct timegates stack: (a) shop RESTOCK timers force a return at a specific clock time to catch rare stock, and (b) offline growth guarantees a reward is waiting, which is the come-back promise. Bee Swarm Simulator (17,137 CCU, 4,492,652,697 visits, 6,484,856 favorites — a 2018 game still running) uses the same skeleton via bear quests with cooldowns and long-horizon hive growth. For the auto-battler: a unit-shop that restocks on a real-world timer (which is already the native TFT/auto-chess shop mechanic!) plus an offline 'training' accrual on benched pieces. Note this hook is native to auto-battlers — the draft shop IS a restock timer.
insights.evidence: Offline growth and shop-restock loop quoted directly from the dev-authored Grow a Garden 2 description via games.roblox.com API. Bee Swarm quest/reward loop also from dev description. All stats as of 2026-07-23.

insights.topic: Social/party play + player-vs-player theft — Steal a Brainrot is the biggest engagement machine on the platform by favorites-per-year
insights.detail: Steal a Brainrot (universe 7709344486): 175,978 CCU, 71,720,800,777 visits — the highest visit count in this entire dataset — and 28,774,510 favorites, on a game created far more recently than Adopt Me. Dev-authored loop: 'Buy a Brainrot / Steal Brainrots from other players / Generate money / Rebirth / Buy slaps and troll gear to troll other players!' The retention engine is that OTHER PLAYERS are the content: your idle income is only safe if you defend it, so leaving the game has a cost, and returning has urgency. Grow a Garden 2 copied this exactly — its description adds 'Make a guild to compete for exclusive weekly rewards!🛡️ But be careful... because at night STEALING STARTS!🌙' — combining a guild/social layer with a nightly PvP-theft window. For a PvE-first auto-battler this is the hook to steal LAST and carefully: a guild/party layer with weekly competitive rewards is low-risk, but asymmetric theft of units would conflict with a PvE-first, young-audience, cosmetics-monetized design.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites from games.roblox.com API 2026-07-23. Steal loop, guild weekly rewards, and nightly stealing window all quoted from dev-authored descriptions returned by the same API call.

insights.topic: Session-count loops — short, repeatable, sub-10-minute rounds are what actually keeps the CCU chart's top slots
insights.detail: The top of Roblox's live 'Top Playing Now' sort on 2026-07-23 is dominated by games with very short or interruption-tolerant sessions: Brookhaven RP 519,057 CCU (drop-in RP, no session), Murder Mystery 2 296,755 (rounds of a few minutes), RIVALS 202,366 (short FPS rounds), Forsaken 99,411, Dress To Impress 88,155 (timed rounds of a few minutes). The Battle Bricks description explicitly sells this property: 'A linear game that you can pick up from any time!' The transferable rule: the auto-battler's unit-draft → position → auto-battle → reward cycle must resolve fast enough that a player can complete one full loop in a single short session and feel a reward land. TFT's ~30-minute match length is the wrong target for Roblox's young mobile-heavy audience — compress to a 3-8 round mini-run.
insights.evidence: CCU rankings and figures are [High], pulled live from the explore-api top-playing-now sort on 2026-07-23. The causal claim that SHORT SESSIONS drive those rankings is my inference from the composition of the list plus the Battle Bricks dev quote — no published per-game session-length data was verified. Blog sources (rolearn.dev, bloxg.com) make the same claim but are [Low] trust.

insights.topic: Battle pass with a 30-day daily-claim track — Blade Ball's seasonal pass is the standard cosmetic-monetization + return-visit combo
insights.detail: Blade Ball (Wiggity.): 13,344 CCU, 6,286,424,436 visits, 12,670,791 favorites (2026-07-23). It runs numbered seasonal Battle Passes (documented through Season 9 'Cyber Pass', plus themed Winter/Easter/Samurai passes) with a free track and a paid Premium track. Reported Premium benefits: increased rewards, extra weekly challenges, and a bonus of 10 free levels. Progression XP comes from eliminations. A 30-day daily-login claim track runs alongside, with milestone unlocks at day 2, day 14, and day 30 (emotes and cosmetics). Note the dev description already lists the monetization surface this project is targeting: 'stand out with a variety of iconic weapon skins and finisher effects' — i.e. paid decorative weapons, exactly the model in the project brief, validated on a 6.3B-visit game. The 'buy 10 free levels' pattern is also the cleanest non-pay-to-win Robux sink.
insights.evidence: CCU/visits/favorites and the weapon-skins/finisher-effects monetization quote are [High], from games.roblox.com API and the dev-authored description on 2026-07-23. Pass season numbering, Premium benefits, and day-2/14/30 milestones come from Blade Ball Fandom wiki and Sportskeeda guides — secondary, well-corroborated, but not primary.

insights.topic: Roblox's Discover algorithm has a dedicated 'Top Revisited' sort — return rate is a distribution lever, not just a revenue lever
insights.detail: The Roblox explore API exposes exactly five game sorts: top-trending, up-and-coming, top-playing-now, fun-with-friends, and top-revisited. 'Top Revisited' is a first-party algorithmic surface that ranks games by players coming BACK, and it visibly promotes small games: on 2026-07-23 it listed Dungeon Quest (OG) at 663 CCU, Rogue Lineage at 1,261, Grave/Digger at 2,065, Fallen Survival at 1,170, and The Battle Bricks at 7,426 — alongside giants like Blox Fruits (212k) and Adopt Me (261k). This is the single most actionable structural finding for a new game: you do not need mega-CCU to get free Roblox distribution, you need high return rate, and Roblox will surface you to new players for it. Every retention hook in this research therefore pays twice — once in retained players, once in algorithmic reach. Also note 'fun-with-friends' exists as its own sort, meaning social/party features are independently rewarded with distribution.
insights.evidence: Sort list retrieved directly from https://apis.roblox.com/explore-api/v1/get-sorts on 2026-07-23 (returned exactly: filters_v5, top-trending, up-and-coming, top-playing-now, fun-with-friends, top-revisited). The low-CCU games listed above were returned by get-sort-content for sortId=top-revisited on the same date. The claim that it ranks on return rate is inferred from the sort's name and its low-CCU composition — Roblox does not publish the ranking formula.

insights.topic: DevEx rate is now two-tier, and the premium tier structurally penalizes a young audience
insights.detail: Roblox pays $0.0038 USD per Earned Robux (standard, since 2025-09-05 10AM PT; Robux earned before that cashes out at the legacy $0.0035). A separate, higher rate of $0.0054 per Robux applies ONLY to spend from age-checked 18+ US players in eligible R15 games, effective 2026-06-08 (a 42% uplift). Roblox's own justification: 'The 18 to 34 user cohort on Roblox is growing over 50% year-over-year in the U.S.-and monetizes 50% higher than the under 18 cohort.' STRATEGIC CONSEQUENCE for this project: the identical Robux spent by a 12-year-old is worth ~30% less in DevEx cash than the same Robux from an age-checked 18+ US player. A deliberately young-audience game is opting into the lower payout tier on every dollar.
insights.evidence: Standard/legacy rates and the 8.5% increase language appear in Roblox Corp's FY2025 Form 10-K; the 18+ tier, +42% figure, R15 requirement, eligible product types (game passes, Robux subscriptions, select in-game items, private servers) and the 2026-06-08 effective date come from Roblox's own newsroom post (April 2026). Corroborated by the DevEx help page.

insights.topic: DevEx eligibility gate: 30,000 Earned Robux minimum, 13+, one cashout per month
insights.detail: To convert Robux to real money you must: be at least 13 years old, hold a minimum of 30,000 Earned Robux, have a Roblox-verified email, a valid DevEx portal account, and filed tax documentation (W-9 US / W-8 non-US), plus be in good standing under the Terms of Use. 30,000 Robux = $114 USD at the standard rate, $162 USD at the 18+ US rate. Payouts run through Tipalti; one cashout request per calendar month; ~10 business days first time, ~5 thereafter. Practical read: the first real payout requires roughly 30,000 Robux of NET earned revenue, i.e. ~42,900 Robux of gross in-game sales after the 30% marketplace fee.
insights.evidence: Roblox help center DevEx page lists eligibility bullets verbatim ('Be at least 13 years old', 'Have a minimum of 30,000 Earned Robux in your account'). Tipalti/monthly-cadence detail from secondary DevEx trackers; treat cadence as [Medium].

insights.topic: AUTHOR-DERIVED: developers capture only ~21-27% of gross consumer spend (~30-38% at the 18+ rate)
insights.detail: Chain: player buys Robux at retail (~$0.0125/R$ at the $9.99/800R$ tier; best case ~$0.0100/R$ at the $99.99/10,000R$ tier) -> creator keeps 70% of the Robux on a developer product or game pass (30% marketplace fee) -> creator converts at DevEx. Math: 0.70 x $0.0038 / $0.0125 = 21.3%; at the $99.99 tier, 0.70 x $0.0038 / $0.0100 = 26.6%. At the 18+ US rate: 30.2% to 37.8%. So Roblox (plus the Apple/Google cut baked into Robux retail pricing) retains roughly 62-79% of every dollar a player spends. Budget and revenue modelling for this project must start from ~$0.22-0.27 per gross consumer dollar, not from Robux face value.
insights.evidence: This is my own calculation, not a Roblox-published figure. The 70% creator share on dev products and passes is well established (unified marketplace fee, effective 2020-04-02, reduced to ~30% for all users). The DevEx rates are primary-sourced. The retail Robux price tiers ($4.99/400, $9.99/800, $19.99/1700, $49.99/4500, $99.99/10000) come from secondary sources only - my direct fetch of roblox.com/upgrades/robux returned navigation chrome, not price data - so the retail input is [Medium].

insights.topic: Revenue distribution is one of the most extreme power laws in games - median DevEx creator made $1,575/year
insights.detail: Roblox's own Annual Economic Impact Report (2025-09-04): 'more than 24,500 are part of our DevEx Program, with the median creator participating in the DevEx Program receiving $1,575 USD during the 12 months ended December 31, 2024.' Same report, 2024 averages: top 1,000 developers $820,000 each; top 100 developers $6,000,000 each; top 10 developers $33,900,000 each. That is a ~21,500x spread between the median DevEx participant and a top-10 studio. FY2025 platform totals (10-K): $1,503.1M paid to creators (up from $922.8M in FY2024); 35,500+ creators qualified for DevEx as of 2025-12-31; 23,500+ actually took payouts during 2025. Naive average payout ($1.5B / 23,500 = ~$64k) is a statistical mirage - the median is 40x lower. Planning assumption: 'real income via DevEx' means landing in the top ~1,000 experiences, not merely shipping a competent game.
insights.evidence: Median and top-N averages are stated directly by Roblox in its own economic impact report; totals and creator counts are from the audited FY2025 10-K. Note the top-N figures are 2024 vintage even in the Sept 2025 report; 2025 figures are likely higher.

insights.topic: Paid Random Items policy: full numeric odds disclosure is mandatory, enforced since 2026-05-26
insights.detail: Roblox's Paid Random Items policy covers anything bought with Robux OR with an in-game currency bought with Robux that yields a randomized outcome: spinning wheels, egg hatching, loot chests/capsules, random enhancement effects, AND probability-modifier items (luck boosts, pity systems). Requirements: display all possible outcomes with actual numerical odds as percentages summing to exactly 100%, BEFORE purchase; when outcomes are too numerous, use a clickable 'Info'/'Details' button (a bare icon is not sufficient); dynamically update odds where a user can only obtain one instance; the same rules apply to indirect purchases (keys, re-roll tokens, spin tickets); luck/odds-augmenting items must show their numeric effect on the adjusted odds. Free randomized rewards are exempt. The clarified requirements went live 2026-05-26; non-compliance is handled through standard moderation with notification and appeal.
insights.evidence: Roblox Creator Hub policy doc plus the official DevForum announcement 'Clarifying Requirements for Paid Random Items' (live 2026-05-26). Quoted requirement: 'Odds disclosures must be shown for each possible item prior to purchase.'

insights.topic: DIRECT ANSWER to the open question: cosmetic-gacha vs unit-gacha makes ZERO regulatory difference
insights.detail: Roblox's Paid Random Items policy draws no distinction whatsoever between pulling a decorative skin and pulling a fighting unit. Both are 'paid random items.' Both carry identical odds-disclosure burden, identical PolicyService age/region gating, and identical moderation exposure. So 'cosmetics-only gacha is the safer choice' is only half true: it is safer on pay-to-win perception and on player-trust/backlash, but it buys you nothing on compliance cost or on the size of your addressable paying audience. The real discriminators between the two designs are (a) pay-to-win optics and review-bomb risk, and (b) IsPaidItemTradingAllowed - Roblox gates peer trading of paid-random outcomes separately, which matters far more if pulls produce tradeable fighting units than if they produce bound cosmetics.
insights.evidence: Derived directly from the policy text, which enumerates capsules, pets, chests, enhancement effects and modifiers as a single category with no cosmetic/functional carve-out, and from the two separate PolicyService flags (ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted, IsPaidItemTradingAllowed).

insights.topic: BIGGEST CONSTRAINT ON THE GACHA THESIS: paid random items are legally blocked for large parts of a young audience
insights.detail: PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync returns ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted per user, based on geolocation, age group and platform. Known restrictions: UK users under 18 (effective 2024-08-13, determined by the account's stated birthday) and ALL Australian users regardless of age (effective 2024-09-20). Roblox's 2026 clarification lists restricted regions as Australia, Belgium, Netherlands, United Kingdom and Brazil. The 10-K notes that in Belgium and the Netherlands loot boxes 'may be considered gambling and are restricted,' and that Australia requires mature ratings. Enforcement is brutal: if you declare paid random items and do NOT implement the API, your experience automatically becomes UNAVAILABLE in those markets. Compliant alternatives Roblox requires you to offer restricted users: unpaid earnable paths, predetermined non-random sequences, direct guaranteed purchase, hiding/removal of the feature, error blocking, or spatial separation. For a young-audience game, this means you must build and maintain a full non-gacha purchase path anyway - which weakens gacha as the primary monetization pillar.
insights.evidence: Two official Roblox DevForum announcements give the UK-under-18 and Australia-all-users rules with dates; the Creator Hub doc enumerates the required compliant alternatives; the FY2025 10-K risk factors confirm Belgium/Netherlands/Australia treatment.

insights.topic: South Korea 확률형 아이템: disclosure regime (2024-03-22), then punitive damages + reversed burden of proof (2025-08-01)
insights.detail: Phase 1: the amended 게임산업진흥에 관한 법률 and its Enforcement Decree (passed 2024-01-02) took effect 2024-03-22, requiring all games offering probability-type items to disclose item types and odds in a form users can readily understand (percentage, fraction, function or text). Item categories are defined as capsule-type (캡슐형), reinforcement-type (강화형), synthesis-type (합성형), and 'other' (quantity/time-limited, probability-variable 확률변동형, and ceiling/pity-type 천장형), each with specific display rules. Non-display or false display triggers a MCST correction recommendation/order; failing a correction order carries up to 2 years imprisonment or a fine up to KRW 20 million. MCST staffed a 24-person monitoring unit. Phase 2: a further amendment promulgated 2025-01-31 and in force since 2025-08-01 adds (a) punitive damages of up to 3x actual damages for intentional concealment or misstatement of odds, and (b) a reversal of the burden of proof - the game company must prove it acted without intent or negligence to escape liability, which raises class-action exposure sharply. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: Korea is a DISCLOSURE regime, not a restriction regime. Korea is not on Roblox's restricted-region list; Korean minors can buy gacha, they just must see the odds.
insights.evidence: Korean government policy briefing (korea.kr) confirms the 2024-03-22 effective date, the item taxonomy, the 2-year/KRW 20M penalty and the monitoring unit. Korean law-firm newsletters (Yulchon/Hwawoo, Lawtimes) and Electronic Times confirm the 2025-01-31 promulgation, 2025-08-01 enforcement, 3x punitive damages and burden-of-proof reversal.

insights.topic: Korea's law is plausibly why odds disclosure went global on Roblox - but Roblox never says so
insights.detail: Trade press (TechTimes, 2026-06-26) frames Roblox's worldwide odds-disclosure requirement as a consequence of Korea's loot-box rules: rather than maintain a Korea-only compliant build, Roblox changed disclosure rules everywhere, so 'players anywhere in the world now see the odds on a paid random item because of a rule written in Seoul.' I could not corroborate the causation from Roblox itself - the official 2026-05-26 announcement does not mention Korea. Treat the causal story as plausible narrative, not established fact. The operative fact (global mandatory numeric disclosure) is independently confirmed and does not depend on this.
insights.evidence: Single secondary source for causation; Roblox's own announcement is silent on Korea.

insights.topic: App-store loot-box rules reach you indirectly, through Roblox, not directly
insights.detail: An individual Roblox experience is never submitted to Apple App Review or Google Play review - Roblox Corp is the app publisher and absorbs those obligations (Apple's guideline 3.1.1 requires disclosure of loot-box odds prior to purchase; Google Play has an equivalent requirement). Roblox discharges them downstream via the Paid Random Items policy and PolicyService flags. Practical consequence: your entire compliance surface for gacha is Roblox's developer policy, not the app store guidelines. But it also means Roblox can tighten those rules unilaterally at any time, with a moderation-first enforcement model, and your monetization design has no appeal to a higher authority.
insights.evidence: Structural inference from the publishing relationship plus Roblox's own policy architecture; the specific Apple/Google guideline numbering is from general knowledge and was not re-verified against the current guideline text in this session.

insights.topic: Game pass vs developer product: the correct mapping for an auto-battler
insights.detail: Game passes are a ONE-TIME Robux purchase granting a permanent privilege (restricted areas, avatar items, permanent power-ups). Developer products are REPEATABLY purchasable (in-game currency, ammo, potions) - the same user can buy the same product many times. Both keep 70% for the creator. Mapping for this project: gacha pulls, pull-currency/gems, energy/refresh, re-roll tokens and battle-pass tier skips = developer products (the repeatable spend engine, and where lifetime value actually accrues). Permanent cosmetic unlocks, permanent board skins, VIP/2x-rewards, early-access units and the battle pass itself = game passes (the one-time, high-ticket, low-friction purchases). Note the 18+ premium DevEx rate explicitly covers 'game passes, Robux subscriptions, select in-game items, and private servers' - Roblox subscriptions are a third lever worth evaluating.
insights.evidence: Definitions from the Creator Hub monetization docs; 70% share from the unified marketplace fee change; eligible-product list from the April 2026 DevEx newsroom post.

insights.topic: Sell cosmetics as in-experience passes/dev products, NOT as catalog UGC - the share difference is 70% vs 30%
insights.detail: Roblox's marketplace fee schedule: for avatar/UGC items sold on the Marketplace the creator receives 30%, scaling up to a maximum 70% only when the item is priced at 6x or more above the price floor. For an in-experience avatar item purchase the split is creator 30% + experience owner 40%. Limited-item resale splits 10% creator / 50% reseller / 10% seller-affiliate / 30% Roblox. Contrast: a game pass or developer product returns a flat 70%. Since this project plans paid decorative weapons and colors, implement them as in-experience game passes or developer products (70%) rather than as catalog UGC accessories (30%), unless you own both the item and the experience, in which case in-experience UGC also reaches 70% combined. Plugins/models are the only category where 'only taxes and payment processing fees are deducted' (and carry a 30-day escrow hold).
insights.evidence: Creator Hub 'Marketplace fees and commissions' doc states the 30% creator / 40% experience owner in-experience split and the 30%-to-70% progressive marketplace scale verbatim.

insights.topic: Named comparable - Anime Vanguards: the closest live analogue (unit gacha + auto-combat)
insights.detail: Anime Vanguards (Kitawari, experience ID 16146832113) is a tower-defense/auto-combat game whose core loop is summoning random units - structurally the nearest thing on Roblox to a unit-gacha auto-battler. Live figures as of 2026-07-23: 1,998,943,435 total visits, 1,972,771 favorites, 2,579,766 likes vs 86,359 dislikes (96.76% rating - exceptionally high), 9,997 concurrent players at snapshot with a 12,952 24-hour peak. For contrast, trade coverage in 2024 reported the game at 220,000+ concurrent users. It reached ~2 billion visits and a near-97% rating in about 2.5 years from a 2024-01-28 creation date, which validates the unit-gacha loop's ability to acquire and convert a huge audience.
insights.evidence: Rolimons live game page for ID 16146832113 (visits, favorites, likes, CCU, 24h peak), fetched 2026-07-23. The 220k CCU 2024 figure is from Pocket Tactics, secondary [Medium]. I attempted RoMonitor's monetization breakdown for this title twice (direct and via r.jina.ai) - it is login-gated, so I have no per-product Robux pricing or revenue estimate for it.

insights.topic: WEAK SIGNAL, do not treat as a genre law: unit-gacha CCU appears to decay far harder than cosmetic/expression CCU
insights.detail: Side-by-side live snapshot, all as of 2026-07-23: Anime Vanguards (unit gacha) 2.00B visits but only ~10.0k CCU; Dress To Impress (cosmetic/expression-led, ID 15101393044) 10.58B visits, 6,996,482 favorites, 3,860,957 likes vs 404,372 dislikes, and 118,766 CCU; Grow a Garden (ID 126884695634066) 35.76B visits, 11,329,621 favorites, 78,243 CCU. Tempting conclusion - cosmetic/expression loops sustain concurrency an order of magnitude better than unit-gacha collection loops - but I am flagging this LOW confidence because of a live confound: the Anime Vanguards snapshot was taken between content events (the experience is titled 'Extermination Event Pt. 1' and was updated 2 days prior), and every event-driven Roblox title spikes and troughs around its update cycle. Game age and update timing are not controlled for, and n=1 per genre. To promote this to a real finding you would need CCU trajectories over several months for 3-5 titles per pattern.
insights.evidence: All three CCU/visit/favorite figures are directly read from Rolimons live game pages on 2026-07-23 and are individually [High]; the cross-genre inference drawn from them is [Low].

insights.topic: Platform-level economics you should model against (FY2025 10-K)
insights.detail: Roblox reported 127 million average DAUs across over 180 countries in 2025. Bookings ran approximately $0.15 per DAU per day, and $10.36 per DAILY PAYING user per day - the gap quantifies how small the paying cohort is relative to total DAU. Roblox recognizes revenue over an estimated average paying-user lifetime of 27 months as of 2025-12-31, which is the platform's own working assumption for how long a paying player stays valuable. Model implication: your revenue is (DAU) x (conversion rate) x (~$10 daily paying-user bookings) x (~22-27% take-home), and the conversion rate is the lever with the widest variance and the one you control through design.
insights.evidence: All figures stated in Roblox Corp Form 10-K for fiscal year ended 2025-12-31.

insights.topic: Mandatory age checks from January 2026 make the under-18 gacha restriction enforceable at platform level
insights.detail: Roblox's FY2025 10-K describes mandatory age-checks beginning January 2026, using facial age estimation, identity verification, and parent/caregiver-provided age data, initially gating chat access. Two consequences for this project: (1) the 18+ premium DevEx rate becomes operable because Roblox can now positively identify age-checked adults; (2) age-based paid-random-item restrictions stop depending on a self-declared account birthday and become enforceable, which means any under-18 gacha restriction Roblox chooses to expand will actually bite. The 10-K also flags Australia's Social Media Minimum Age Act (under-16 ban on certain platforms) and parallel US/EU legislative efforts as active risks. Planning stance: assume the direction of travel is MORE age-gating of paid randomness for minors, not less, and do not build a business model whose survival depends on under-18 gacha spend remaining legal in your key markets.
insights.evidence: Risk-factor and business-description language in the FY2025 10-K, including the specific age-check methodologies and the Australian statute.

Pet Simulator 99 — 163,141 CCU / 2.558B visits, "2,000+ pets to collect". Sol's RNG — 31,010 CCU / 2.022B visits, roll-only loop + luck potions. RIVALS — 202,868 CCU / 16.78B visits / 84.76M favorites, discrete ~2–3mo ranked seasons. Blade Ball — 13,344 CCU / 6.286B visits, full Elo reset per season with rank-gated skins. Murder Mystery 2 — 296,610 CCU / 27.59B visits (2014 game, still). Adopt Me! — 261,565 CCU / 44.20B visits. Anime Defenders — 3.430B visits at **394 CCU**.

## 2. The Gap

**What exists on Roblox:** dozens of *path/lane* auto-fight games (Anime Expeditions, Vanguards, UTDZ, ASTD, all TD derivatives) and one grid-placement variant that scaled (Garden Tower Defense). What exists on the *loop* side: Anime Squadron's "plan your lineup" pre-battle phase and Anime Card Clash's roll→deck→auto-fight, both of which reached only 6–8K CCU and neither of which sells **positional skill** as the core fantasy.

**What does not exist:** a Roblox game where **spatial arrangement on a bounded board is the primary skill expression and the primary progression axis**, married to an **Elo ladder with seasonal reset**. Every scaled title in the set resolves player agency into *which unit you own*, not *where you put it* — placement is a throughput puzzle against a fixed path, so the meta is a gacha meta. That is exactly why they decay: when the answer is "own the 0.005% unit," the game is over once you own it (Anime Defenders: 3.43B visits → 394 CCU).

**The unoccupied position:** *chess as the skill layer, gacha as the cosmetic/variant layer.* Four concrete openings:
1. **Board positioning as the win condition** — no scaled Roblox competitor uses adjacency/line-of-attack/flanking as the decision surface. Garden TD proves the grid is not a comprehension barrier for the audience; nobody has made the grid *matter*.
2. **Elo is native, and unclaimed in this genre.** RIVALS (202,868 CCU) and Blade Ball (13,344 CCU) prove Roblox kids accept seasonal rank resets; zero unit-collector auto-battlers in this set run a real ladder. Chess players already accept Elo as legitimate — you inherit the mental model free.
3. **Evergreen IP.** Every competitor above 100K CCU rents a meme (Skibidi, brainrot) or an anime license. Toilet TD's `[LEGACY]` tag is what renting looks like at end of lease. Chess costs nothing, ages never, and is globally pre-taught.
4. **Player-as-piece.** The brief's own hook — the avatar *is* the piece — is absent from every title in the set. It converts every cosmetic SKU into something the player literally embodies on the board, which is what makes cosmetic-first monetization viable (TDS's 4.9B-visit template).

**Honest counter:** the gap may be unoccupied because it doesn't sell. Battle Pet is the nearest structural attempt — 157,828 likes but **445 CCU**. Players enjoy the auto-battler shape and leave. The gap is real; the burden of proof is retention, not novelty.

## 3. Roblox-Specific Retention Hooks (ranked)

1. **Seasonal Elo ladder with hard reset + rank-gated cosmetic.** Proof: Blade Ball resets every player's Elo to Rookie at season start and gates unique Sword Skins behind Champion / global-leaderboard placement (13,344 CCU / 6.286B visits); RIVALS runs Seasons 0–3 at ~2–3mo each with rewards keyed to highest rank reached and soft placement carry-over (202,868 CCU / 84.76M favorites) (sources: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=6035872082,4777817887 as of 2026-07-23; season mechanics from https://bladeball.fandom.com/wiki/Ranked and https://robloxrivals.fandom.com/wiki/Ranked_Seasons — community wikis, mechanic corroborated, **no published uplift figure**). **Adapt:** 8-week seasons, full Elo reset, one rank-gated piece skin per season per tier. This is the most native-fitting hook in the entire set and it feeds the cosmetics line directly.
2. **Collection surface area / an index you can never finish.** Proof: Pet Simulator 99 — "✨ Currently 2,000+ pets to collect!" at 163,141 CCU / 2.558B visits; Sol's RNG — "400+ unique auras" at 31,010 CCU / 2.022B visits (source: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=3317771874,5361032378, as of 2026-07-23). **Adapt:** 6 piece types × N skins × rarity tiers = a completion grid with a visible denominator. Ship the dex UI in v1; the number of collectibles *is* the retention surface.
3. **The pull itself as a loop, with luck sold as the accelerant.** Proof: Sol's RNG reduced the game to press-Roll-get-aura and still hit 2.02B visits; its dev description sells "potions to increase your luck". Anime Card Clash monetizes the same way via Luck / Cooldown tracks. **Adapt:** sell the **luck multiplier and the extra pull**, never the guaranteed unit. This is the single most important pattern in this document — it keeps the compulsion loop while dodging the pay-to-win read that will otherwise poison the ladder.
4. **Return-rate over raw scale — the algorithm rewards it.** Proof: The Battle Bricks (7,420 CCU, single-player unit-draft auto-battler, explicitly Battle Cats-inspired) surfaced in Roblox's own `top-revisited` sort — Roblox's algorithmic label for games players come back to (source: https://apis.roblox.com/explore-api/v1/get-sort-content?sortId=top-revisited, as of 2026-07-23). **Adapt:** optimize D1/D7 return, not CCU spikes. `top-revisited` placement is free distribution and it is the metric DevEx actually pays on.
5. **Daily login streak — table stakes, do not build it.** Roblox ships a first-party **Engagement Rewards** feature package with client+server logic, default UI, Time and Daily reward types, `isHiddenOnJoin` auto-popup, `isAlignedToStreakResetTime`, and a documented day-1→day-7 escalation example (source: https://create.roblox.com/docs/resources/feature-packages/engagement-rewards, as of 2026-07-23). ⚠ **The docs publish no retention statistics** — the uplift is inference. **Adapt:** drop the package in, spend zero engineering on it, spend all effort on reward *contents* (pull tickets, cosmetic shards).
6. **Trading — strongest long-tail hook, free to operate, highest regulatory risk.** Proof: Murder Mystery 2 (2014) at 296,610 CCU / 27.59B visits and Adopt Me! at 261,565 CCU / 44.20B visits are both trading economies; MM2's friction-light trade UX spawned an out-of-game value ecosystem (Traderie, Dexerto value lists) that pulls players back in (sources: https://games.roblox.com/v1/games?universeIds=383310974,66654135 as of 2026-07-23; trade UX/value-list detail from secondary guides, **unverified**). **Adapt — with a hard constraint:** trading + paid gacha in one game is a loot-box-with-cash-out structure aimed at minors. If trading ships, **cosmetics only, and anything obtained from a paid pull is permanently untradeable.**
7. **Timed multiplier events on a visible cadence.** Weakest-evidenced tier here (Brainrot TD bakes "2x diamond" into its title at 693 CCU; Grow a Garden's published weekly calendar was cited but arrived truncated — treat as **unverified**). **Adapt:** publish a weekly event calendar out-of-game; cheap to run, gives Discord/YouTube something to cover.

## 4. Monetization Playbook

**Base SKUs (ship all of these regardless of the gacha decision):**
- **Piece skins** — the core cosmetic. Player-as-piece means every skin is worn, seen by opponents, and visible on the board every round. Tiered crates on the TDS model (Basic buyable with earned currency, Premium/Deluxe with Robux), with published rarity tables.
- **Board / VFX / capture-animation skins** — second cosmetic axis, near-zero balance risk.
- **Season Pass** (~400–800 Robux) keyed to the 8-week Elo season — recurring revenue that scales with the retention hook rather than fighting it.
- **Luck & extra-pull SKUs** — the Anime Card Clash / Sol's RNG pattern. Sells *odds*, not outcomes.
- **Event-exclusive crates that never re-release** — TDS's Bunny/Spooky FOMO mechanic, 7 years of evidence.
- **Roblox Premium payout bonus** — Anime Card Clash grants Premium players Luck/Cooldown bonuses; free incremental revenue via Premium Payouts.

### The Gacha Decision

**(a) Cosmetics-only gacha.** Evidence for: Tower Defense Simulator, cosmetic-first crates, **7 years, 4.865B visits, and a *stable* 21,357 CCU in 2026**. That is the only title in this entire set that has neither collapsed nor spiked — cosmetic-only correlates with flat, durable revenue. Evidence against: ARPDAU ceiling is materially lower, and Anime Card Collection (142M visits in ~7 months on pure pull-and-collect) shows a weak pull layer loses the acquisition race outright.

**(b) Units-in-gacha with F2P grind + pity + published odds.** Evidence for: Anime Vanguards, 2.0B visits / 1.97M favorites, with a verified 0.005% chase rate and a 20,000-summon one-time pity — that is the shape this audience tolerates and pays into. Evidence against, and it is severe: Anime Defenders sits at **394 CCU on 3.430B lifetime visits**; All Star Tower Defense at ~1,395 CCU on 7.875B. Unit-gacha games monetize violently then die. DevEx income tracks the spike years, not the tail — which is *tolerable* if you accept a 12–24 month revenue window, and fatal if you want a business.

**Recommendation: (b), with a mandatory competitive carve-out.**

Run unit gacha — pulls yield fighting pieces, with rarity tiers, pity, and a guaranteed F2P grind path — **but scope paid power strictly to the PvE ladder.** Ranked PvP draws from a **normalized shared pool**: every player enters ranked with the full roster available, so Elo measures positioning, never wallet. Sell luck, pull volume, cosmetics, and the Season Pass into that structure.

Justification:
- Cosmetics-only (a) is the safe answer and it caps you near TDS's profile — 21K CCU after *seven years* of live-ops. The brief asks for real DevEx income, and the acquisition data (Anime Card Collection, Sol's RNG) says the pull *is* the acquisition engine on Roblox. Shipping without a unit pull surrenders the top of the funnel.
- The decay in (b) is not caused by unit gacha per se; it is caused by **the gacha being the entire meta**. When owning the 0.005% unit is the win condition, completing the collection is the exit. A chess ladder gives players a reason to log in that gacha cannot exhaust — and the seasonal reset (Blade Ball / RIVALS pattern) manufactures a re-grind the roster alone never provides. This is the specific mechanism that decouples you from the Anime Defenders curve.
- The carve-out neutralizes the P2W read where it costs most. A ranked ladder that money can buy is worthless as a retention hook, and worthless as a marketing story.

**Regulatory work required for (b) — non-negotiable:**
- **Published probability disclosure.** Korea's Game Industry Promotion Act probability-disclosure mandate requires in-game and store-page odds disclosure for paid random items [Medium confidence — statutory requirement, **not verified in this research pass; get legal review before launch**]. Build the odds table as data, render it in-client, and version it per banner — retrofitting this later is expensive.
- **Pity must be published, not just implemented.** Anime Vanguards's disclosed 20,000-summon pity is what makes a 0.005% rate socially acceptable.
- **Paid-pull items are permanently untradeable.** Non-negotiable if trading ever ships (see hook #6).
- **No Robux→tradeable-value path, ever.** That is the structure regulators target hardest with a minor audience.

## 5. Minimal Addictive Core Loop

The MVP's only job is to answer one question: *does board positioning produce a compulsion to replay?* Everything that is not that question is cut — no gacha, no shop, no PvP, no seasons, no meta-progression beyond a single visible dex counter. Ship a single-player PvE run: the player drafts from a small offered set of chess pieces, places them on a bounded grid, presses Fight, watches a fully deterministic auto-resolve, and either advances to a harder wave or dies and restarts. Draft offers are randomized per round so the positioning problem is never the same twice — that RNG is the pull mechanic, delivered free, which is the cheapest possible test of whether the compulsion exists before any Robux code is written. Instrument exactly three things: **rounds per session, restart-after-loss rate, and D1/D7 return.** If restart-after-loss is weak, positioning is not fun and no monetization layer will save it — kill the project there rather than after the economy is built. Benchmark against Battle Pet's failure signature (high likes, 445 CCU): loved on first contact, abandoned by day two.

**The loop:**
- **Offer** — 3 random pieces from a pool of ~12, player picks 1 (this is the pull, unmonetized)
- **Place** — position owned pieces on a small grid (start 5×5); adjacency and line-of-attack must visibly change outcomes
- **Fight** — deterministic auto-resolve, ~20–30s, no player input
- **Reward** — gold + a dex entry unlock on win; visible "N / total collected" counter
- **Escalate** — next wave is harder; run ends on loss
- **Restart** — one tap, back to Offer with a fresh randomized pool

Skipped: gacha, Robux SKUs, PvP, Elo, seasons, trading, daily rewards. Add gacha and the ladder only after restart-after-loss and D7 clear the bar — the Roblox Engagement Rewards package covers dailies in an afternoon whenever you want it.

## 6. Top Risks

- **Gacha decay is the base case, not the tail risk.** Anime Defenders: 3.430B visits → **394 CCU**. All Star Tower Defense: 7.875B visits → ~1,395 CCU. Anime Vanguards: 2.0B visits → 10,060 CCU. Every unit-gacha title in this set is on the same curve. The seasonal-Elo layer is the *only* proposed mitigation, and it is unproven in combination with unit gacha on Roblox. If it fails, you get a 12–18 month revenue window and then a `[LEGACY]` tag.
- **Retention, not acquisition, is the killer — and the nearest structural comp already failed it.** Battle Pet: 157,828 likes, 23.4M visits, **445 CCU**. Players like auto-battlers on contact and do not stay. Assume you will reproduce this unless the MVP metrics say otherwise.
- **Pay-to-win poisons the one native hook.** Chess's entire value here is that Elo is credible. Any leakage of paid power into ranked destroys that credibility, and with it the seasonal-reset engine, the leaderboard, and the reason to log in on day 60. The normalized-pool carve-out must be a launch constraint, not a v2 fix.
- **Regulation on units-in-gacha with a minor audience.** Korean probability-disclosure obligations [Medium, unverified — needs legal review], plus loot-box scrutiny generally, plus Roblox's own policy surface. The lethal combination is paid gacha + trading; if both ship, paid-pull items must be permanently untradeable. Budget real legal time, and build the odds table as versioned data from day one.
- **Discovery in a saturated niche.** Anime Paradox X (1,137 CCU) is the median 2025-cohort outcome; Anime Squadron (~8K CCU in <1yr) is a good one; Anime Expeditions' 180,904 CCU is a **peak snapshot** and arithmetically inconsistent with its own visit history [Medium] — do not put it in a forecast. Chess has no meme velocity, so paid UGC/influencer distribution and `top-revisited` placement carry the whole load.
- **Design risk on the load-bearing assumption.** The claim that Garden Tower Defense proves grid placement works for this audience is an **unverified gameplay reading** of a game whose metrics were confirmed but whose mechanics were not. Play it and confirm before the board design depends on it — and separately validate that *positioning* (not just grid placement) reads as fun to a 10-year-old, which no title in this set demonstrates.
